results.title: 均场变分后验与逐层替代模型
results.statement_tex: \theta^*=\arg\min_\theta\mathrm{KL}[q_\theta(W)\Vert p(W\mid D)],\quad p(y\mid x)=E_{W\sim q_\theta}p(y\mid x,W)

definitions.name: 本条局部对象
definitions.body_md: $W$ 收集网络权重，$q_\theta(W)=\mathcal N(W;\mu,\Sigma)$，$\Sigma$ 对角、$\theta=(\mu,\Sigma)$；$D$ 为训练集。替代标准DNN参数 $\psi$ 取BNN权重与偏置均值；其输入及低层特征另加独立对角Gaussian扰动。

results.original_statement_md:
Unlike standard DNNs, a BNN represents each weight in the network as a probability distribution, instead of a scalar. In this paper, we limit the scope of our study to mean-field variational BNNs (Blundell et al., 2015), where all weights $W$ are formulated as a Gaussian distribution $\mathcal N(W;\mu,\Sigma)$, and the covariance matrix $\Sigma$ is diagonal. Other types of BNNs (e.g., BNNs based on the Monte Carlo Dropout (Gal & Ghahramani, 2016)) are not discussed. The BNN learns parameters $\theta=(\mu,\Sigma)$, and we use $q_\theta(W)$ to represent the weight distribution. Let us consider a classification task with the training data $D=\{(\mathbf x^{(1)},y^{(1)}),\ldots,(\mathbf x^{(n)},y^{(n)})\}$. Training a BNN is to minimize the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence between the distribution $q_\theta(W)$ and the posterior distribution $p(W\mid D)$.
$$\begin{aligned}\theta^*&=\arg\min_\theta\mathrm{KL}[q_\theta(W)\Vert p(W\mid D)]\\&=\arg\min_\theta\{-E_{W\sim q_\theta(W)}[\log p(D\mid W)]+\mathrm{KL}[q_\theta(W)\Vert p(W)]\}.\quad\text{(1)}\end{aligned}$$
where the first term is the classification loss, and the second term is the KL divergence between $q_\theta(W)$ and the prior distribution $p(W)$, which is usually formulated as a Gaussian distribution $\mathcal N(W;0,\mathbf I)$. In addition, given a testing sample $\mathbf x$, the inference of the BNN is conducted as follows. First, network weights are sampled from the weight distribution $q_\theta(W)$ to construct multiple neural networks. Then, each network is used to conduct inference on the sample $\mathbf x$, and the final inference result $p(y\mid\mathbf x)$ is computed as the average classification probability of all the networks,
$$p(y\mid\mathbf x)=E_{W\sim q_\theta(W)}[p(y\mid\mathbf x,W)].\quad\text{(2)}$$
Implementation details of the experiment in Section 2.2 of the main paper. In Section 2.2 of the main paper, we minimized the KL divergence between the feature distribution in the surrogate DNN model and the feature distribution in the BNN. The feature distributions in the surrogate DNN model and in the BNN were not Gaussian distributions. Therefore, the KL divergence between the feature distributions did not have a close-form formula. To facilitate the optimization, we simply used two Gaussian distributions to approximate the feature distributions in the surrogate DNN model and in the BNN, and optimized the KL divergence between the two Gaussian distributions. Besides, we did not consider the dependency between different feature dimensions to simplify the computation.

results.title: 原始交互与全部掩码重构
assumptions: 只需有限集合游戏；不要求可微、不要求稀疏，也不要求输出基线为零。

definitions.name: 本条局部对象
definitions.body_md: 有限总体为 $N$；固定样本、输入基线后，$g(T)=v(x_T)$、$b=g(\varnothing)$，原 $I(S\mid x)$ 对应 $I_g(S)$。$\Omega\subseteq2^N$ 是允许保留的支持族；完整重构可取全部集合，或包含所有非零系数的族。

results.original_statement_md:
Specifically, the interaction effect $I(S\mid\mathbf x)$ on the sample $\mathbf x$ is computed by the Harsanyi dividend (Harsanyi, 1963).
$$I(S\mid\mathbf x)=\sum_{T\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|T|}\cdot v(\mathbf x_T).\quad\text{(3)}$$
If $I(S\mid\mathbf x)$ has a significant value, then the neural network is considered to encode an interactive concept $S$; otherwise, if $I(S\mid\mathbf x)\approx0$, the concept $S$ does not exist. Here, $\mathbf x_T$ denotes the masked input sample, where variables in $N\setminus T$ are masked and variables in $T$ are kept unchanged. Besides, $v(\mathbf x_T)\in\mathbb R$ can be computed as a scalar output of the neural network on the masked sample $\mathbf x_T$ (e.g., the confidence score of classifying the input sample $\mathbf x_T$ to the ground-truth category $v(\mathbf x_T)=\log\frac{p(y=y^{truth}\mid\mathbf x_T)}{1-p(y=y^{truth}\mid\mathbf x_T)}$).

Faithfulness of interactive concepts. Given an input sample $\mathbf x$ with $n$ variables, we have $2^n$ different ways to mask the sample $\mathbf x$ and obtain the masked sample $\mathbf x_T$ w.r.t. all subsets $T\subseteq N$. To this end, Ren et al. (2021) proved that
$$\exists\Omega\subseteq2^N,\ \text{s.t.}\ \forall T\subseteq N,\quad v(\mathbf x_T)=\sum_{S\in\Omega,S\subseteq T}I(S\mid\mathbf x).\quad\text{(4)}$$
where $2^N=\{S\mid S\subseteq N\}$. The equation indicates that interactive concepts in $\Omega$ can well mimic network outputs on all the $2^n$ masked samples. Thus, we can consider that all interactive concepts in the set $\Omega$ as faithful inference patterns encoded by the neural network.

results.title: 外引稀疏概念的范围
assumptions: 保留作者“通常”与外引语境；本篇没有陈述逐游戏的明确稀疏界及其完整技术前提。

definitions.name: 本条局部对象
definitions.body_md: 显著族由固定样本交互强度筛选；“稀疏”指相对全部 $2^n$ 个支持只保留少量。正文分别引用faithfulness、稀疏AND表示以及图1的概念出现现象。Appendix B是已有研究综述，不包含本地七性质列表。

results.original_statement_md:
However, recent studies have empirically discovered (Ren et al., 2023a; Li & Zhang, 2023) and theoretically proved (Ren et al., 2023c) that sparse AND relationships between input variables were usually implicitly encoded by a neural network when it was sufficiently trained. As shown in Figure 1(a), these AND relationships can be viewed as specific types of interactive concepts, which will be introduced in the interactive concepts paragraph.

Sparsity of interactive concepts. More crucially, extensive experiments (Ren et al., 2023a; Li & Zhang, 2023) discovered that interactive concepts emerging in a neural network are usually very sparse. Figure 1(b) shows that most interactive concepts have near-zero interaction effects ($|I(S\mid\mathbf x)|\approx0$), thus having negligible influence on the network output. Only a few salient interactive concepts have significant effects $I(S\mid\mathbf x)$ on the network output. In this way, the network output can be mimicked by only a few salient interactive concepts in $\Omega_{salient}$.

Ren et al. (2023a) used game-theoretic interactions to analyze the emergence of concepts in the training of neural networks, and proved the faithfulness and sparsity of such formulation of concepts. In this paper, we follow the definition of concepts in Ren et al. (2023a), and prove BNNs’ tendency to avoid encoding high-order (complex) concepts.

definitions.name: 本条局部对象
definitions.body_md: $r$ 是输入基线向量，$z_i=x_i-r_i$，$\pi\in\mathbb N^N$，$\operatorname{supp}\pi=\{i:\pi_i>0\}$。$a_\pi=D^\pi v(r)/\pi!$。原 $U_{S,\pi}(x\prime)$ 含随输入变动的符号，$J$ 使用绝对增量；两者相乘才是有符号单项式。

results.original_statement_md:
Lemma 2.1. Given a neural network $v$ and an arbitrary input sample $\mathbf x'\in\mathbb R^n$, the network output can be decomposed using the Taylor expansion $v(\mathbf x')=\sum_{S\subseteq N}\sum_{\boldsymbol\pi\in Q_S}U_{S,\boldsymbol\pi}\cdot J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x')$. In this way, according to Eq. (3) in the main paper, the interaction effect $I(S\mid\mathbf x')$ on the sample $\mathbf x'$ can be reformulated as

$$I(S\mid\mathbf x')=\sum_{\boldsymbol\pi\in Q_S}U_{S,\boldsymbol\pi}\cdot J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x'),\qquad\text{(20)}$$

where $J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x')=\prod_{i\in S}\left(\operatorname{sign}(x'_i-r_i)\cdot\frac{x'_i-r_i}\tau\right)^{\pi_i}$ denotes an expansion term of the degree $\boldsymbol\pi$, $\boldsymbol\pi\in Q_S=\{[\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_n]\mid\forall i\in S,\pi_i\in\mathbb N^+;\forall i\notin S,\pi_i=0\}$. $U_{S,\boldsymbol\pi}=\frac{\tau^m}{\prod_{i=1}^n\pi_i!}\frac{\partial^m v(\mathbf x_\varnothing)}{\partial x_1^{\pi_1}\cdots\partial x_n^{\pi_n}}\cdot\prod_{i\in S}[\operatorname{sign}(x'_i-r_i)]^{\pi_i}$, $m=\sum_{i=1}^n\pi_i$.
results.original_proof_md:
Proof. Let us denote the function on the right of Eq. (20) by $\widetilde I(S\mid\mathbf x')$, i.e.,

$$\widetilde I(S\mid\mathbf x')=\sum_{\boldsymbol\pi\in Q_S}U_{S,\boldsymbol\pi}J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x').\qquad\text{(21)}$$

We need to prove that for any arbitrary input sample $\forall\mathbf x'\in\mathbb R^n$, $\widetilde I(S\mid\mathbf x')=I(S\mid\mathbf x')$.

Actually, it has been proven in Grabisch & Roubens (1999) and Ren et al. (2023a) that the Harsanyi dividend $I(S\mid\mathbf x')$ is the unique metric satisfying the faithfulness requirement mentioned in the main paper, i.e., satisfying

$$\forall T\subseteq N,\quad v(\mathbf x'_T)=\sum_{S\in\Omega,\,S\subseteq T}I(S\mid\mathbf x').\qquad\text{(22)}$$

Thus, as long as we can prove that $\widetilde I(S\mid\mathbf x')$ also satisfies the above faithfulness requirement, we can obtain $\widetilde I(S\mid\mathbf x')=I(S\mid\mathbf x')$.

To this end, we only need to prove $\widetilde I(S\mid\mathbf x')$ also satisfies the faithfulness requirement in Eq. (22). Specifically, given an input sample $\forall\mathbf x'\in\mathbb R^n$, let us consider the Taylor expansion of the network output $v(\mathbf x_T)$ of an arbitrarily masked sample $\mathbf x'_T$ ($T\subseteq N$), which is expanded at $\mathbf x'_\varnothing=[r_1,\ldots,r_n]$. Then, we have

$$\forall T\subseteq N,\quad v(\mathbf x'_T)=\sum_{\pi_1=0}^\infty\sum_{\pi_2=0}^\infty\cdots\sum_{\pi_n=0}^\infty\frac1{\prod_{i=1}^n\pi_i!}\frac{\partial^m v(\mathbf x'_\varnothing)}{\partial x_1^{\pi_1}\cdots\partial x_n^{\pi_n}}\cdot\prod_{i=1}^n[(\mathbf x'_T)_i-r_i]^{\pi_i}.\qquad\text{(23)}$$

where $\boldsymbol\pi\in\{[\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_n]\mid\forall i\in N,\pi_i\in\mathbb N\}$ denotes the degree vector of Taylor expansion terms, and $m=\sum_{i=1}^n\pi_i$. In addition, $r_i$ denotes the reference value to mask the input variable $x_i$.

According to the definition of the masked sample $\mathbf x'_T$, we have that all variables in $T$ keep unchanged and other variables are masked to the reference value. That is, $\forall i\in T,(\mathbf x'_T)_i=x_i;\forall i\notin T,(\mathbf x'_T)_i=r_i$. Hence, we obtain $\forall i\notin T,[(\mathbf x'_T)_i-r_i]^{\pi_i}=0$. Then, among all Taylor expansion terms, only terms corresponding to degrees $\boldsymbol\pi$ in the set $P=\{[\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_n]\mid\forall i\in T,\pi_i\in\mathbb N;\forall i\notin T,\pi_i=0\}$ may not be zero. Therefore, Eq. (23) can be re-written as

$$\forall T\subseteq N,\quad v(\mathbf x'_T)=\sum_{\boldsymbol\pi\in P}\frac1{\prod_{i=1}^n\pi_i!}\frac{\partial^m v(\mathbf x'_\varnothing)}{\partial x_1^{\pi_1}\cdots\partial x_n^{\pi_n}}\cdot\prod_{i\in T}(x'_i-r_i)^{\pi_i}.\qquad\text{(24)}$$

We find that the set $P$ can be divided into multiple disjoint sets as follows, $P=\bigcup_{S\subseteq T}Q_S$, where $Q_S=\{[\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_n]\mid\forall i\in S,\pi_i\in\mathbb N^+;\forall i\notin S,\pi_i=0\}$. Then, we can derive that

$$\begin{aligned}
\forall T\subseteq N,\quad v(\mathbf x'_T)&=\sum_{S\subseteq T}\sum_{\boldsymbol\pi\in Q_S}\frac1{\prod_{i=1}^n\pi_i!}\frac{\partial^m v(\mathbf x'_\varnothing)}{\partial x_1^{\pi_1}\cdots\partial x_n^{\pi_n}}\cdot\prod_{i\in S}(x'_i-r_i)^{\pi_i}\\
&=\sum_{S\subseteq T}\sum_{\boldsymbol\pi\in Q_S}\underbrace{\frac{\tau^m}{\prod_{i=1}^n\pi_i!}\frac{\partial^m v(\mathbf x'_\varnothing)}{\partial x_1^{\pi_1}\cdots\partial x_n^{\pi_n}}\prod_{i\in S}(\delta_i)^{\pi_i}}_{\text{termed }U_{S,\boldsymbol\pi}}\cdot\underbrace{\prod_{i\in S}\left(\delta_i\frac{x'_i-r_i}\tau\right)^{\pi_i}}_{\text{termed }J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x')},\quad\text{(25)}
\end{aligned}$$

where $\tau\in\mathbb R$ is a pre-defined constant and $\delta_i=\operatorname{sign}(x_i-r_i)\in\{-1,1\}$ is a sign function and it satisfies $\prod_{i\in S}(\delta_i)^{2\pi_i}=1$. Then, Eq. (25) can be re-written as

$$\forall T\subseteq N,\quad v(\mathbf x'_T)=\sum_{S\subseteq T}\sum_{\boldsymbol\pi\in Q_S}U_{S,\boldsymbol\pi}\cdot J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x')=\sum_{S\subseteq T}\widetilde I(S\mid\mathbf x').\qquad\text{(26)}$$

Thus, $\widetilde I(S\mid\mathbf x')$ satisfies the faithfulness requirement in Eq. (22) when $\Omega=2^N$.

Therefore, Lemma 1 holds.

en.title: The valid scope of Taylor support expansion
en.overview: Take the allowed one-dimensional ReLU network $v(t)=\max(t-1/2,0)$, baseline $r=0$ and input $x=1$. Every classical Taylor coefficient at zero vanishes, yet $I_g(\{1\})=v(1)-v(0)=1/2$. Thus the unrestricted global expansion fails for arbitrary DNNs. This is a complete human-readable network counterexample; the machine evidence does not formalize the ReLU counterexample.
assumptions: Retain the source quantifier over arbitrary neural networks. The valid finite component concerns an actual finite polynomial. An infinite series also needs convergence at all relevant masks and legitimate regrouping, which the source does not supply.

results.original_statement_md:
Lemma 2.1 provides a new perspective to analyze the sensitivity of the interaction effect $I(S)$. In particular, just like in Ren et al. (2023a) and Ren et al. (2023b), we mask the input variable $x_i$ by setting it to its reference value $x_i\leftarrow r_i$. The reference value $r_i$ is designed as follows. Let $E_x[x_i]$ denote the average value of the input variable $x_i$ over all input samples, which is usually regarded as a no-information state of this input variable (Ancona et al., 2019). In this paper, we remove the information from the input variable $x_i$ by pushing $x_i$ by a large enough distance $\tau$ towards its mean value. In other words, if $x_i>E_x[x_i]$, we set the reference value $r_i=x_i-\tau$; otherwise, $r_i=x_i+\tau$. Here, $\tau\in\mathbb R$ is a pre-defined constant. In this way, compared to setting $r_i=E_x[x_i]$, the above setting ensures comparable perturbation magnitudes over different input dimensions.

Furthermore, in order to simplify the proof, when we add a small Gaussian perturbation $\boldsymbol\epsilon\sim\mathcal N(\mathbf0,\sigma^2\mathbf I)$ to the sample $\mathbf x$, we ignore the extremely low possibility of large perturbations $|\epsilon_i|\ge\tau$ because the variance $\sigma^2$ is small.

Footnote 1: We need to avoid the case of over-perturbation, by setting $r_i\leftarrow\max(r_i,E_x[x_i])$, if $x_i>E_x[x_i]$; $r_i\leftarrow\min(r_i,E_x[x_i])$, otherwise. However, such cases are not common in real applications, so we ignore such settings in the following analysis.
results.overview: 若 $x_i>E[x_i]$，脚注可用 $r_i=\max\{x_i-\tau,E[x_i]\}$；否则用 $r_i=\min\{x_i+\tau,E[x_i]\}$。裁剪后实际距离可能小于τ。作者后续忽略这一处理，理论式采用严格距离τ；重写和机器模型明确使用该简化范围。

en.title: Exact Gaussian moments of the actual lowest-degree dividend
en.overview: For $v(x_T\prime)=b+a\prod_{i\in S}(x_i\prime-r_i)\mathbf1_{i\in T}$, the support identity makes the nonempty dividend exactly $a\prod_{i\in S}(x_i\prime-r_i)$. The two sign powers in source $U(x\prime)J_{abs}(x\prime)$ cancel and recover the actual signed polynomial even after crossing the baseline.
assumptions: Use the source lowest-term hypothesis and fixed reference-distance model, with $\tau\ne0$ and independent $\epsilon_i\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)$. Do not treat the moving-sign coefficient $U(x\prime)$ as constant across inputs. Gaussian tails are not truncated.

definitions.name: Local objects for this entry
definitions.body_md: Fix a nonempty concept $S$, lowest-monomial coefficient $a$, and increments $x_i-r_i=s_i\tau$ with $s_i^2=1$. The actual lowest dividend is $I(x\prime)=a\prod_{i\in S}(x_i\prime-r_i)$, and $U_{\mathrm{ref}}=a\prod_{i\in S}s_i\tau=I(x)$. An arbitrary constant output baseline $b$ is retained; it contributes no nonempty dividend.

proof_steps.title: Extract the lowest dividend from actual masks
proof_steps.body_md: For $v(x_T\prime)=b+a\prod_{i\in S}(x_i\prime-r_i)\mathbf1_{i\in T}$, the support identity makes the nonempty dividend exactly $a\prod_{i\in S}(x_i\prime-r_i)$. The two sign powers in source $U(x\prime)J_{abs}(x\prime)$ cancel and recover the actual signed polynomial even after crossing the baseline.

proof_steps.title: Factor using the fixed reference coefficient
proof_steps.body_md: Coordinatewise factorization gives $I(x+\epsilon)=U_{\mathrm{ref}}\prod_{i\in S}(1+s_i\epsilon_i/\tau)$. Since $s_i^2=1$, the Gaussian map-law gives $s_i\epsilon_i/\tau\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2/\tau^2)$; measurable coordinate transforms preserve independence. This expression uses no approximation of absolute-value tails.

proof_steps.title: Compute moments from the actual Gaussian laws
proof_steps.body_md: Each shifted factor has finite second moment, mean one and raw second moment $1+\sigma^2/\tau^2$. Independence gives product mean one and raw second moment $(1+\sigma^2/\tau^2)^{|S|}$. Scaling by $U_{\mathrm{ref}}$ and subtracting the mean square yields the source moments. $U_{\mathrm{ref}}=0$ and $\sigma=0$ are allowed because neither is divided out.

notation_map.note: Canonical scalar b is the fully masked output, distinct from layer biases b^(l).
The dividend transforms the complete v, not an AND/OR component.
The fixed input distance in the simplified model; experiments use 0.5.
Independent centered Gaussian input noise, distinct from sampled BNN weights.
Lowest-dividend moments allow zero noise; ordinary growth ratios require positive noise.
Positive integer degrees on the support and zero elsewhere.
The appendix uses signs at reference x_i; the Lemma coefficient definition also contains current x′ signs, kept distinct.
The source definition implicitly depends on current input and is not constant over all x′.
Sign times increment is its absolute value; odd signed moments differ.
Theorem 2.2’s moments are faithfully interpreted using the coefficient at reference x; ambiguity against the moving-sign Lemma definition is recorded.

assumptions: 数学式在有限一、二阶矩范围解释；论文实际 Gaussian 整数幂因子满足这些条件，ConceptGaussian 从分布律证明，而非将矩公式作为假设。

definitions.name: 本条局部对象
definitions.body_md: $X_i$ 是同一概率空间上的有限独立随机变量族。均值与方差是 Lebesgue 积分；方差定义为 $E(X_i-EX_i)^2$。

results.original_statement_md: Proposition G.1. If random variables $X_1,X_2,\cdots,X_k$ are independent of each other, then $\mathbb E[X_1X_2\cdots X_k]=\prod_{i=1}^k\mathbb E[X_i]$, and $\operatorname{Var}[X_1X_2\cdots X_k]=\prod_{i=1}^k(\mathbb E[X_i]^2+\operatorname{Var}[X_i])-\prod_{i=1}^k\mathbb E[X_i]^2$.
results.overview: 可测独立变量的乘积积分分解给 $E\prod_iX_i=\prod_iEX_i$。平方后的族仍独立；有限 L2 因子及其独立乘积具有所需可积性，故 $E(\prod_iX_i)^2=\prod_iEX_i^2$。

proof_steps.title: 分别分解一次与二次乘积积分
proof_steps.body_md: 可测独立变量的乘积积分分解给 $E\prod_iX_i=\prod_iEX_i$。平方后的族仍独立；有限 L2 因子及其独立乘积具有所需可积性，故 $E(\prod_iX_i)^2=\prod_iEX_i^2$。

proof_steps.title: 减去均值平方并适配 Gaussian 幂
proof_steps.body_md: 代入 $EX_i^2=(EX_i)^2+\operatorname{Var}X_i$，再减去 $(E\prod_iX_i)^2=\prod_i(EX_i)^2$。本篇 $X_i=|1+s_i\epsilon_i/\tau|^{\pi_i}$；Gaussian 任意有限 Lp 矩通过幂变换给每个因子 L2，因此原概率模型所需条件被实际满足。

en.title: Actual integral moments of an independent product
en.overview: Factorization for measurable independent variables gives $E\prod_iX_i=\prod_iEX_i$. The squared family remains independent. Finite L2 factors and their independent product supply the required integrability, so $E(\prod_iX_i)^2=\prod_iEX_i^2$.
assumptions: Interpret the formulas where the first and second moments are finite. The paper’s Gaussian integer-power factors satisfy these conditions, which ConceptGaussian proves from their distribution laws.

proof_steps.title: Factor the first and second product integrals
proof_steps.body_md: Factorization for measurable independent variables gives $E\prod_iX_i=\prod_iEX_i$. The squared family remains independent. Finite L2 factors and their independent product supply the required integrability, so $E(\prod_iX_i)^2=\prod_iEX_i^2$.

proof_steps.title: Subtract the mean square and adapt Gaussian powers
proof_steps.body_md: Substitute $EX_i^2=(EX_i)^2+\operatorname{Var}X_i$ and subtract $(E\prod_iX_i)^2=\prod_i(EX_i)^2$. Here $X_i=|1+s_i\epsilon_i/\tau|^{\pi_i}$. Arbitrary finite Gaussian Lp moments and the power transform give L2 for each factor, discharging the required premises in the paper’s model.

en.title: Absolute triggers and signed moments differ
en.overview: Coordinatewise, $J=\prod_i|Z_i|^{\pi_i}$. Actual Gaussian laws give finite second moments of all powers. Independent-product formulas yield $EJ=\prod_im_i$ and $\operatorname{Var}J=\prod_i(m_i^2+d_i)-\prod_im_i^2$. If all degrees are even, absolute and signed powers agree pointwise, so the source replacement is exact on that subdomain.
assumptions: Use independent untruncated Gaussian noise and a fixed nonzero reference distance. Retain arbitrary positive integer degrees. The author explicitly neglects low-probability baseline crossing, without an exact tail-error bound.

definitions.body_md: The nonempty concept has positive integer degrees on its support. Source $J$ contains $\operatorname{sign}(x_i\prime-r_i)(x_i\prime-r_i)=|x_i\prime-r_i|$, while its signed comparison factor is $Z_i=1+s_i\epsilon_i/\tau$. Put $m_i=E|Z_i|^{\pi_i}$ and $d_i=\operatorname{Var}|Z_i|^{\pi_i}$.

proof_steps.title: Recover exact moments of the original absolute trigger
proof_steps.body_md: Coordinatewise, $J=\prod_i|Z_i|^{\pi_i}$. Actual Gaussian laws give finite second moments of all powers. Independent-product formulas yield $EJ=\prod_im_i$ and $\operatorname{Var}J=\prod_i(m_i^2+d_i)-\prod_im_i^2$. If all degrees are even, absolute and signed powers agree pointwise, so the source replacement is exact on that subdomain.

proof_steps.title: Give an exact counterexample using the original one-coordinate trigger
proof_steps.body_md: Take $x=1,r=0,\tau=1,\pi=1$ and $\epsilon\sim\mathcal N(0,q)$ with $q>0$. The original trigger is $J=|1+\epsilon|$. The signed mean is $E(1+\epsilon)=1$, while $E|1+\epsilon|=1+2E[-(1+\epsilon)\mathbf1_{\epsilon<-1}]>1$ because a nondegenerate Gaussian has positive density there. The machine proof uses mutual absolute continuity with Lebesgue measure and the continuous nonzero function $|z|-z$ to establish the strict difference. The squares agree pointwise, so the actual variance $1+q-(E|1+\epsilon|)^2<q$ also differs from the signed variance.

proof_steps.title: Distinguish the actual dividend from its absolute trigger
proof_steps.body_md: This counterexample concerns $J$ in Theorem 2.3, not the actual lowest dividend in Theorem 2.2. In the latter, moving-sign coefficients cancel the trigger signs, giving the exact fixed-reference signed product. The absolute trigger alone has no such cancellation. Neglecting tails as an approximation does not make the two exact moments equal.

assumptions: 原独立 Gaussian、正整数支持次数和包含关系保留。原比值的有定义域要求 $S\ne\varnothing$、$\sigma>0$ 及非零距离；实际 adapter 使用 $\tau>0$。零噪声或空旧支持使方差分母为零，单列定义域缺口，不把有效主干判为错误。

definitions.name: 本条局部对象
definitions.body_md: $S\subsetneq S\prime$，旧坐标次数不变。$A=J_S$、$B=\prod_{i\in S\prime\setminus S}|Z_i|^{\pi_i\prime}$、$J_{S\prime}=AB$，$Z_i\sim\mathcal N(1,q)$、$q=\sigma^2/\tau^2$。$K_T=|EJ_T|/\operatorname{Var}J_T$，分母是方差而不是标准差。

results.original_proof_md:
Proof. According to Theorem 2.3, we have

$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[J(S',\boldsymbol\pi'\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]
&=\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon\left[\prod_{i\in S'}\left(1+\frac{\epsilon_i}\tau\right)^{\pi'_i}\right]\\
&=\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon\left[\prod_{i\in S}\left(1+\frac{\epsilon_i}\tau\right)^{\pi'_i}\prod_{i\in S'\setminus S}\left(1+\frac{\epsilon_i}\tau\right)^{\pi'_i}\right]\qquad\text{// }S\subsetneq S'\\
&=\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon\left[\underbrace{\prod_{i\in S}\left(1+\frac{\epsilon_i}\tau\right)^{\pi_i}}_A\underbrace{\prod_{i\in S'\setminus S}\left(1+\frac{\epsilon_i}\tau\right)^{\pi'_i}}_B\right]\qquad\text{// }\forall i\in S,\pi'_i=\pi_i\\
&=\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[AB]\\
&=(\mathbb E_\epsilon^{,2}[A]+\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[A])(\mathbb E_\epsilon^{,2}[B]+\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[B])-\mathbb E_\epsilon^{,2}[A]\mathbb E_\epsilon^{,2}[B]\\
&\qquad\text{// A and B are independent; Proposition G.1}\\
&=\mathbb E_\epsilon^{,2}[A]\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[B]+\mathbb E_\epsilon^{,2}[B]\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[A]+\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[A]\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[B]\\
&>\mathbb E_\epsilon^{,2}[B]\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[A]+\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[A]\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[B].\quad\text{(40)}
\end{aligned}$$

Therefore, we can prove the first equality as follows.

$$\begin{aligned}
\frac{\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[J(S',\boldsymbol\pi'\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]}{\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]}
&=\frac{\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[AB]}{\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[A]}\\
&>\mathbb E_\epsilon^{,2}[B]+\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[B]\\
&>\mathbb E_\epsilon^{,2}[B]\\
&=\mathbb E_\epsilon^{,2}\left[\prod_{i\in S'\setminus S}\left(1+\frac{\epsilon_i}\tau\right)^{\pi'_i}\right]\\
&=\prod_{i\in S'\setminus S}\mathbb E_{\epsilon_i}^{,2}\left[\left(1+\frac{\epsilon_i}\tau\right)^{\pi'_i}\right]\\
&\qquad\text{// }\epsilon_i\text{ is independent of each other; Proposition G.1}.\quad\text{(41)}
\end{aligned}$$

Furthermore, we have

$$\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_\epsilon[J(S',\boldsymbol\pi'\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]
&=\mathbb E_\epsilon\left[\prod_{i\in S'}\left(1+\frac{\epsilon_i}\tau\right)^{\pi'_i}\right]\\
&=\mathbb E_\epsilon\left[\prod_{i\in S}\left(1+\frac{\epsilon_i}\tau\right)^{\pi'_i}\prod_{i\in S'\setminus S}\left(1+\frac{\epsilon_i}\tau\right)^{\pi'_i}\right]\qquad\text{// }S\subsetneq S'\\
&=\mathbb E_\epsilon\left[\prod_{i\in S}\left(1+\frac{\epsilon_i}\tau\right)^{\pi_i}\prod_{i\in S'\setminus S}\left(1+\frac{\epsilon_i}\tau\right)^{\pi'_i}\right]\qquad\text{// }\forall i\in S,\pi'_i=\pi_i\\
&=\mathbb E_\epsilon[AB].\quad\text{(42)}
\end{aligned}$$

and also

$$\mathbb E_\epsilon[J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]=\mathbb E_\epsilon\left[\prod_{i\in S}\left(1+\frac{\epsilon_i}\tau\right)^{\pi_i}\right]=\mathbb E_\epsilon[A].\qquad\text{(43)}$$

Therefore, we have

$$\frac{\mathbb E_\epsilon[J(S',\boldsymbol\pi'\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]}{\mathbb E_\epsilon[J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]}=\frac{\mathbb E_\epsilon[AB]}{\mathbb E_\epsilon[A]}=\mathbb E_\epsilon[B].\qquad\text{(44)}$$

Then, we can prove the second inequality as follows.

$$\begin{aligned}
&\frac{\mathbb E_\epsilon[J(S',\boldsymbol\pi'\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]/\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[J(S',\boldsymbol\pi'\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]}{\mathbb E_\epsilon[J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]/\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]}\\
&=\frac{\mathbb E_\epsilon[B]}{\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[AB]/\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[A]}\\
&<\frac{\mathbb E_\epsilon[B]}{\mathbb E_\epsilon^{,2}[B]}\\
&=\frac{1}{\mathbb E_\epsilon[B]}\\
&=\frac{1}{\mathbb E_\epsilon\left[\prod_{i\in S'\setminus S}\left(1+\frac{\epsilon_i}\tau\right)^{\pi'_i}\right]}\\
&=\frac{1}{\prod_{i\in S'\setminus S}\mathbb E_{\epsilon_i}\left[\left(1+\frac{\epsilon_i}\tau\right)^{\pi'_i}\right]}.\quad\text{(45)}
\end{aligned}$$

Moreover, we can prove that $\mathbb E_{\epsilon_i}[(1+\frac{\epsilon_i}\tau)^k]\ge1,\forall k\in\mathbb N^+$, i.e., $\mathbb E[X^k]\ge1$, where $X\sim\mathcal N(1,(\sigma/\tau)^2)$.

For a random variable following a Gaussian distribution $\widetilde X\sim\mathcal N(\widetilde\mu,\widetilde\sigma^2)$, Willink (2005) proved the following property:

$$\mathbb E[\widetilde X^{k+1}]=\widetilde\mu\mathbb E[\widetilde X^k]+k\widetilde\sigma^2\mathbb E[\widetilde X^{k-1}].\qquad\text{(46)}$$

Now let us consider $X\sim\mathcal N(1,(\sigma/\tau)^2)$. We have $\mathbb E[X^{k+1}]=\mathbb E[X^k]+k(\sigma/\tau)^2\mathbb E[X^{k-1}]$. By induction, it is easy to prove that $\mathbb E[X^k]\ge\mathbb E[X]=1$.
results.overview: 对 $Z\sim\mathcal N(1,q)$，反射 $Z\mapsto2-Z$ 同律。二项式展开中 $z^k+(2-z)^k\ge2$：令 $t=z-1$，奇次项相消、偶次项非负，常数项为2。积分得 $EZ^k\ge1$；逐点 $|z|^k\ge z^k$ 给 $E|Z|^k\ge EZ^k\ge1$。任意 Gaussian 整数幂均 L2。若 $q>0,k>0$ 且绝对幂方差为零，则它几乎处处为常数；其每个水平集最多两个点，与 Gaussian 无原子矛盾，故方差严格正。独立乘积公式继而给非空积的正方差。

proof_steps.title: 按独立新增坐标精确分解方差
proof_steps.body_md: 记 $a=EA$、$b_B=EB$、$v_A=\operatorname{Var}A$、$v_B=\operatorname{Var}B$。支持不交且坐标独立给 $EAB=ab_B$ 与 $\operatorname{Var}(AB)=v_A(b_B^2+v_B)+a^2v_B$。在上述域 $a\ge1,b_B\ge1,v_A>0,v_B>0$，所以 $\operatorname{Var}(AB)/v_A>b_B^2$。令 $p=\prod_{i\in S\prime\setminus S}EZ_i^{\pi_i\prime}$，有 $b_B\ge p\ge1$，从而原方差下界成立。原 Theorem2.3 的错误精确矩替换不再作为推理前提。

proof_steps.body_md: 由于期望均正，$K_{S\prime}/K_S=b_Bv_A/\operatorname{Var}(AB)<1/b_B\le1/p\le1$。实际 Lean 用整个旧/新增坐标 Gaussian 家族的积分证明两项不等式，所有正方差与矩下界均已由分布律消去，不假设待证结论。$S=\varnothing$ 时 $J_S=1$，$\sigma=0$ 时全部触发恒1；原比值均含0分母。源文未给该边界的实数约定，因此不将 Lean 的总除法零值作为作者约定。

en.title: Nested-support growth of the original absolute trigger
en.overview: For $Z\sim\mathcal N(1,q)$, reflection $Z\mapsto2-Z$ preserves the law. The binomial expansion gives $z^k+(2-z)^k\ge2$: with $t=z-1$, odd terms cancel, even terms are nonnegative and the constant term is two. Integration yields $EZ^k\ge1$. Pointwise $|z|^k\ge z^k$ gives $E|Z|^k\ge EZ^k\ge1$. Every Gaussian integer power is L2. If $q>0,k>0$ and the absolute power had zero variance, it would be almost surely constant. Each level set contains at most two points, contradicting the absence of Gaussian atoms. Its variance is therefore positive; the independent-product formula gives positive variance for every nonempty product.
assumptions: Retain the source independent Gaussian model, positive support degrees and inclusion relation. The ordinary defined ratio domain requires nonempty $S$, positive noise and nonzero distance; the actual adapter uses $\tau>0$. Zero noise or an empty old support yields a zero variance denominator, recorded separately without refuting the valid main comparison.

proof_steps.title: Prove moment lower bounds and nondegeneracy from Gaussian laws
proof_steps.body_md: For $Z\sim\mathcal N(1,q)$, reflection $Z\mapsto2-Z$ preserves the law. The binomial expansion gives $z^k+(2-z)^k\ge2$: with $t=z-1$, odd terms cancel, even terms are nonnegative and the constant term is two. Integration yields $EZ^k\ge1$. Pointwise $|z|^k\ge z^k$ gives $E|Z|^k\ge EZ^k\ge1$. Every Gaussian integer power is L2. If $q>0,k>0$ and the absolute power had zero variance, it would be almost surely constant. Each level set contains at most two points, contradicting the absence of Gaussian atoms. Its variance is therefore positive; the independent-product formula gives positive variance for every nonempty product.

proof_steps.title: Decompose variance using independent added coordinates
proof_steps.body_md: Write $a=EA$, $b_B=EB$, $v_A=\operatorname{Var}A$ and $v_B=\operatorname{Var}B$. Disjoint supports and independent coordinates give $EAB=ab_B$ and $\operatorname{Var}(AB)=v_A(b_B^2+v_B)+a^2v_B$. On the stated domain, $a\ge1,b_B\ge1,v_A>0,v_B>0$, so $\operatorname{Var}(AB)/v_A>b_B^2$. For $p=\prod_{i\in S\prime\setminus S}EZ_i^{\pi_i\prime}$, we have $b_B\ge p\ge1$, proving the source variance lower bound. The incorrect exact moment replacement in Theorem 2.3 is not used as a premise.

proof_steps.title: Compute the stability ratio and check boundaries
proof_steps.body_md: All means are positive, so $K_{S\prime}/K_S=b_Bv_A/\operatorname{Var}(AB)<1/b_B\le1/p\le1$. Actual Lean integrals of the complete old/added Gaussian coordinate family prove both inequalities, with positive variances and moment lower bounds discharged from distribution laws. If $S=\varnothing$, then $J_S=1$; if $\sigma=0$, all triggers equal one. Both cases give zero denominators. The source supplies no ordinary-real convention there, and Lean’s total division is not treated as an author convention.

To facilitate the analysis, we first simplify the conceptual learning as a linear problem. Specifically, we first rewrite the interaction effect of an interactive concept $S$. Given an input sample $\mathbf x$, according to Eq. (8), the interaction effect of the concept $S$ on the sample $\mathbf x'$ (obtained by applying some transformations on $\mathbf x$), $I(S\mid\mathbf x')$, can be rewritten as
$$I(S\mid\mathbf x')=U_S\cdot C_S(\mathbf x').\quad\text{(12)}$$
where the constant $U_S=I(S\mid\mathbf x)$ denotes the interaction effect of the concept $S$, and the function for the activation state is given as $C_S(\mathbf x')=\sum_{\boldsymbol\pi\in Q_S}U_{S,\boldsymbol\pi}J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x')/U_S$.

definitions.body_md: 有限索引 $i$ 对应作者概念 $S$，$C_i$ 是固定的随机特征函数，$w_i$ 对应作者优化变量 $U_S$，$y^*$ 是固定标签。$a,d,w\in\mathbb R^k$；矩阵 $K=\operatorname{diag}d+aa^\top$。$L(w)=E(y^*-\sum_iw_iC_i)^2$ 是原期望平方损失。

results.original_statement_md:
Theorem 2.5. Given two random interactive concepts $S$ and $S'$, we can roughly assume that $C_S(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)$ is independent of $C_{S'}(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)$, because the two concepts $S$ and $S'$ usually have little overlap in most cases. Let $\mathbb E_\epsilon[C_S(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]$ and $\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[C_S(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]$ denote the mean and the variance of $C_S(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)$ w.r.t. $\boldsymbol\epsilon$, respectively. Then, the solution to Eq. (15) in the main paper satisfies the following property:

$$\forall S\in\Omega,\quad |U_S^*|\propto\left|\mathbb E_\epsilon[C_S(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]/\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[C_S(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]\right|.\qquad\text{(47)}$$
results.original_proof_md:
Proof. Let $p=|\Omega|$. Let $\mathbf C(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)=[C_{S_1}(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon),\ldots,C_{S_p}(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]^\top$ denote the vector of all $C_S(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon),S\in\Omega$, and let $\mathbf U=[U_{S_1},\ldots,U_{S_p}]^\top$ denote the vector of all coefficients $U_S,S\in\Omega$. To further simplify the notation, we simply use $\mathbf C$ to denote the random vector $\mathbf C(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)$. Besides, since we assume that each dimension of the vector $\mathbf C(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)$ is independent of each other, we can use $\mathbb E_\epsilon[\mathbf C]=[\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_p]^\top\in\mathbb R^p$ and $\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[\mathbf C]=\operatorname{diag}(\beta_1^2,\ldots,\beta_p^2)\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}$ to denote the mean vector and covariance matrix of the random vector $\mathbf C(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)$, respectively. We prove this theorem in three steps.

Step 1. We first prove that the optimal solution to Eq. (15) in the main paper is given by

$$\forall1\le i\le p,\quad U_{S_i}^*=\frac{1}{\det M}\det(\mathbf M_1,\ldots,\mathbf M_{i-1},\boldsymbol\rho,\mathbf M_{i+1},\ldots,\mathbf M_p).\qquad\text{(48)}$$

where $M=\mathbb E_\epsilon[\mathbf C]\mathbb E_\epsilon[\mathbf C]^\top+\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[\mathbf C]$, $\boldsymbol\rho=y^*\mathbb E_\epsilon[\mathbf C]$, and $\mathbf M_j$ denotes the $j$-th column of the matrix $M$.

We can rewrite the objective function in Eq. (15) in the main paper as

$$\min_{\mathbf U}\mathbb E_\epsilon[(y^*-\mathbf U^\top\mathbf C(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon))^2].\qquad\text{(49)}$$

To minimize the loss $\mathcal L=\mathbb E_\epsilon[(y^*-\mathbf U^\top\mathbf C)^2]$, we set the gradient of the loss w.r.t $\mathbf U$ to zero, i.e.,

$$\begin{aligned}
\nabla_{\mathbf U}\mathcal L&=\mathbb E_\epsilon[2\mathbf C(\mathbf U^\top\mathbf C-y^*)]\\
&=2\mathbb E_\epsilon[\mathbf C\mathbf C^\top\mathbf U-y^*\mathbf C]\\
&=2\mathbb E_\epsilon[\mathbf C\mathbf C^\top]\mathbf U-2y^*\mathbb E_\epsilon[\mathbf C]\\
&=2(\mathbb E_\epsilon[\mathbf C]\mathbb E_\epsilon[\mathbf C]^\top+\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[\mathbf C])\mathbf U-2y^*\mathbb E_\epsilon[\mathbf C]=0.\quad\text{(50)}
\end{aligned}$$

$$\Rightarrow(\mathbb E_\epsilon[\mathbf C]\mathbb E_\epsilon[\mathbf C]^\top+\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[\mathbf C])\mathbf U=y^*\mathbb E_\epsilon[\mathbf C].\qquad\text{(51)}$$

Let $M=\mathbb E_\epsilon[\mathbf C]\mathbb E_\epsilon[\mathbf C]^\top+\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[\mathbf C]$, and $\boldsymbol\rho=y^*\mathbb E_\epsilon[\mathbf C]$. By Cramer's rule, we can obtain the solution to Eq. (51):

$$\forall1\le i\le p,\quad U_{S_i}^*=\frac1{\det M}\det(\mathbf M_1,\ldots,\mathbf M_{i-1},\boldsymbol\rho,\mathbf M_{i+1},\ldots,\mathbf M_p).$$

where $\mathbf M_j$ denotes the $j$-th column of the matrix $M$.

Step 2. We prove that for the optimal solution $\mathbf U^*$, we have

$$\forall1\le i,j\le p,\quad\frac{|U_{S_i}^*|}{|U_{S_j}^*|}=\frac{|\mathbb E_\epsilon[C_{S_i}(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]/\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[C_{S_i}(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]|}{|\mathbb E_\epsilon[C_{S_j}(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]/\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[C_{S_j}(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]|}.\qquad\text{(52)}$$

Since $M=\mathbb E_\epsilon[\mathbf C]\mathbb E_\epsilon[\mathbf C]^\top+\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[\mathbf C]$, we can obtain the $j$-th column of $M$ as

$$\mathbf M_j=\alpha_j\mathbb E_\epsilon[\mathbf C]+\mathbf V_j.\qquad\text{(53)}$$

where $\mathbb E_\epsilon[\mathbf C]=[\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_p]^\top$, and $\mathbf V_j=[0,\ldots,\beta_j^2,\ldots,0]^\top$.

According to the conclusion in Step 1, we have

$$|U_{S_i}^*|=\left|\frac1{\det M}\right|\cdot|\det(\mathbf M_1,\ldots,\mathbf M_{i-1},\boldsymbol\rho,\mathbf M_{i+1},\ldots,\mathbf M_{j-1},\mathbf M_j,\mathbf M_{j+1},\ldots,\mathbf M_p)|.\qquad\text{(54)}$$

$$|U_{S_j}^*|=\left|\frac1{\det M}\right|\cdot|\det(\mathbf M_1,\ldots,\mathbf M_{i-1},\mathbf M_i,\mathbf M_{i+1},\ldots,\mathbf M_{j-1},\boldsymbol\rho,\mathbf M_{j+1},\ldots,\mathbf M_p)|.\qquad\text{(55)}$$

We know that exchanging the rows or columns of a matrix only changes the sign of the determinant of the matrix, but does not change the absolute value of the determinant. Therefore, we have

$$\begin{aligned}
|U_{S_i}^*|&=\left|\frac1{\det M}\right|\cdot|\det(\mathbf M_j,\boldsymbol\rho,\mathbf M_1,\ldots,\mathbf M_{i-1},\mathbf M_{i+1},\ldots,\mathbf M_{j-1},\mathbf M_{j+1},\ldots,\mathbf M_p)|\\
&=\left|\frac1{\det M}\right|\cdot|\det(\mathbf M_j,\boldsymbol\rho,M_{\mathrm{others}})|\quad\text{// Let }M_{\mathrm{others}}\text{ denote the third to the last column}\\
&=\left|\frac1{\det M}\right|\cdot|\det(\alpha_j\mathbb E_\epsilon[\mathbf C]+\mathbf V_j,y^*\mathbb E_\epsilon[\mathbf C],M_{\mathrm{others}})|\quad\text{// Eq. (53)}\\
&=\left|\frac1{\det M}\right|\cdot\left|\underbrace{\det(\alpha_j\mathbb E_\epsilon[\mathbf C],y^*\mathbb E_\epsilon[\mathbf C],M_{\mathrm{others}})}_{=0}+\det(\mathbf V_j,y^*\mathbb E_\epsilon[\mathbf C],M_{\mathrm{others}})\right|\\
&\quad\text{// The determinant is 0 if two columns are linearly dependent}\\
&=\left|\frac1{\det M}\right|\cdot|\det(\mathbf V_j,y^*\mathbb E_\epsilon[\mathbf C],M_{\mathrm{others}})|\\
&=\left|\frac1{\det M}\right|\cdot\left|\det\begin{bmatrix}
0&y^*\alpha_1&\alpha_1\alpha_1+\beta_1^2&\cdots&\alpha_1\alpha_p\\
\vdots&&&&\\
0&y^*\alpha_i&\alpha_i\alpha_1&\cdots&\alpha_i\alpha_p\\
\vdots&&&&\\
\beta_j^2&y^*\alpha_j&\alpha_j\alpha_1&\cdots&\alpha_j\alpha_p\\
\vdots&&&&\\
0&y^*\alpha_p&\alpha_p\alpha_1&\cdots&\alpha_p\alpha_p+\beta_p^2
\end{bmatrix}\right|\\
&=\left|\frac1{\det M}\right|\cdot\left|\det\begin{bmatrix}
\beta_j^2&y^*\alpha_j&\alpha_j\alpha_1&\cdots&\alpha_j\alpha_p\\
0&y^*\alpha_i&\alpha_i\alpha_1&\cdots&\alpha_i\alpha_p\\
0&y^*\alpha_1&\alpha_1\alpha_1+\beta_1^2&\cdots&\alpha_1\alpha_p\\
\vdots&&&&\\
0&y^*\alpha_p&\alpha_p\alpha_1&\cdots&\alpha_p\alpha_p+\beta_p^2
\end{bmatrix}\right|\quad\text{// Exchange rows}\\
&=\left|\frac{\alpha_i}{\det M}\right|\cdot\left|\det\begin{bmatrix}
\beta_j^2&y^*\alpha_j&\alpha_j\alpha_1&\cdots&\alpha_j\alpha_p\\
0&y^*&\alpha_1&\cdots&\alpha_p\\
0&y^*\alpha_1&\alpha_1\alpha_1+\beta_1^2&\cdots&\alpha_1\alpha_p\\
\vdots&&&&\\
0&y^*\alpha_p&\alpha_p\alpha_1&\cdots&\alpha_p\alpha_p+\beta_p^2
\end{bmatrix}\right|\quad\text{// Extract out }\alpha_i\\
&=\left|\frac{\alpha_i\beta_j^2}{\det M}\right|\cdot|\det M'|.\quad\text{(56)}
\end{aligned}$$

where

$$M'=\begin{bmatrix}
y^*&\alpha_1&\cdots&\alpha_p\\
y^*\alpha_1&\alpha_1\alpha_1+\beta_1^2&\cdots&\alpha_1\alpha_p\\
\cdots&&&\\
y^*\alpha_p&\alpha_p\alpha_1&\cdots&\alpha_p\alpha_p+\beta_p^2
\end{bmatrix}.\qquad\text{(57)}$$

Similarly, we can prove that

$$|U_{S_j}^*|=\left|\frac{\alpha_j\beta_i^2}{\det M}\right|\cdot|\det M'|.\qquad\text{(58)}$$

Therefore, we have

$$\forall1\le i,j\le p,\quad\frac{|U_{S_i}^*|}{|U_{S_j}^*|}=\frac{|\alpha_i/\beta_i^2|}{|\alpha_j/\beta_j^2|}=\frac{|\mathbb E_\epsilon[C_{S_i}(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]/\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[C_{S_i}(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]|}{|\mathbb E_\epsilon[C_{S_j}(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]/\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[C_{S_j}(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]|}.$$

Step 3. Based on Step 2, we can directly prove that for the optimal solution $\mathbf U^*$, we have

$$\forall S\in\Omega,\quad |U_S^*|\propto\left|\mathbb E_\epsilon[C_S(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]/\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[C_S(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]\right|.\qquad\text{(59)}$$

proof_steps.body_md: 中心化 $\eta_i=C_i-a_i$，两两独立性与有限 L2 给 $E\eta_i=0$ 和交叉协方差0。于是 $L(w)=(y^*-a^\top w)^2+\sum_i d_iw_i^2=(y^*)^2+w^\top Kw-2y^*a^\top w$。这是原随机特征的积分恒等式，不预设正规方程。

proof_steps.title: 验证显式候选与正定性
proof_steps.body_md: $d_i>0$ 时对任意非零 $h$，$h^\top Kh=\sum_id_ih_i^2+(a^\top h)^2>0$。设 $t=\sum_i a_i^2/d_i\ge0$、$\lambda=y^*/(1+t)$，令 $w_i^*=\lambda a_i/d_i$。直接计算 $a^\top w^*=\lambda t$，故 $(Kw^*)_i=d_iw_i^*+a_i(a^\top w^*)=a_i\lambda(1+t)=y^*a_i$。无需 Cramer 行列式的省略步骤。

proof_steps.title: 完成平方证明唯一最优并保留零方差缺口
proof_steps.body_md: $L(w)-L(w^*)=(w-w^*)^\top K(w-w^*)>0$ 对 $w\ne w^*$ 成立，因此显式解是唯一全局最优，而非仅驻点。绝对值给 $|w_i^*|=|\lambda||a_i/d_i|$，正是共同尺度比例。若两个允许特征都恒1且 $y^*=1$，损失为 $(1-w_1-w_2)^2$，整条直线都最优，而原 $a_i/d_i$ 是1/0；源未排该域，不用严格正方差修订冒充无条件结论。

en.title: The actual global optimum of independent-feature regression
en.overview: Center $\eta_i=C_i-a_i$. Pairwise independence and finite L2 give $E\eta_i=0$ and zero cross-covariances. Thus $L(w)=(y^*-a^\top w)^2+\sum_i d_iw_i^2=(y^*)^2+w^\top Kw-2y^*a^\top w$. This is an integral identity for the actual random features, not an assumed normal equation.
assumptions: Retain the explicitly assumed pairwise feature independence and the defined first and second moments. The ordinary ratio domain requires $d_i>0$. Small typical concept overlap does not prove independence. Features remain fixed during this analysis; their Taylor coefficients are not reoptimized together with the weights.

definitions.name: Local objects for this entry
definitions.body_md: The finite index $i$ corresponds to a source concept $S$. Each $C_i$ is a fixed random feature, $w_i$ is source optimization variable $U_S$, and $y^*$ is the fixed label. Vectors $a,d,w\in\mathbb R^k$ give matrix $K=\operatorname{diag}d+aa^\top$. The source expected squared loss is $L(w)=E(y^*-\sum_iw_iC_i)^2$.

proof_steps.title: Expand the actual loss into mean error and variance penalty
proof_steps.body_md: Center $\eta_i=C_i-a_i$. Pairwise independence and finite L2 give $E\eta_i=0$ and zero cross-covariances. Thus $L(w)=(y^*-a^\top w)^2+\sum_i d_iw_i^2=(y^*)^2+w^\top Kw-2y^*a^\top w$. This is an integral identity for the actual random features, not an assumed normal equation.

proof_steps.title: Verify the explicit candidate and positive definiteness
proof_steps.body_md: If $d_i>0$, every nonzero $h$ satisfies $h^\top Kh=\sum_id_ih_i^2+(a^\top h)^2>0$. Put $t=\sum_i a_i^2/d_i\ge0$, $\lambda=y^*/(1+t)$ and $w_i^*=\lambda a_i/d_i$. Directly, $a^\top w^*=\lambda t$, so $(Kw^*)_i=d_iw_i^*+a_i(a^\top w^*)=a_i\lambda(1+t)=y^*a_i$. No omitted Cramer-determinant argument is needed.

proof_steps.title: Complete the square and retain the zero-variance boundary
proof_steps.body_md: For $w\ne w^*$, completing the square gives $L(w)-L(w^*)=(w-w^*)^\top K(w-w^*)>0$. The candidate is the unique global optimum, rather than merely stationary. Taking absolute values yields $|w_i^*|=|\lambda||a_i/d_i|$, the stated common-scale proportionality. If two allowed features are constantly one and $y^*=1$, then $L(w)=(1-w_1-w_2)^2$ and a whole line minimizes it, while source $a_i/d_i$ is 1/0. This omitted domain is retained; the strictly positive-variance result does not replace an unrestricted claim.

The denominator is variance, not standard deviation; zero variance has no implicit extension.
Local a_i is the source trigger expectation and cannot automatically be dropped across concepts.
G.5 uses b_S for variance; canonical d_i distinguishes it from output baseline b.

assumptions: 原比值的普通实数域：$U\ne0$、$\operatorname{Var}C>0$，并保留 $A_{\min}\le|U|\le A_{\max}$。族为空时极值也需约定；原文没有将这些边界全部排除。

definitions.body_md: $I=UC$，$U=I(S\mid x)$ 是固定参考系数；$A_{\min}$、$A_{\max}$ 是所比较概念族的最小/最大 $|U|$。$C$ 为随机触发，$I$ 为同一随机触发的常数倍。

results.original_statement_md:
Theorem 2.6. Let $A^{\min}=\min_S|U_S|$ and $A^{\max}=\max_S|U_S|$ denote the lower bound and the upper bound of $|U_S|$ over all interactive concepts $S$. Then, for any $S\subseteq N$, we have

$$A^{\min}\cdot\frac{|\mathbb E_\epsilon[I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]|}{\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]}\le\frac{|\mathbb E_\epsilon[C_S(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]|}{\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[C_S(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]}\le A^{\max}\cdot\frac{|\mathbb E_\epsilon[I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]|}{\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]}.\qquad\text{(60)}$$
results.original_proof_md:
Proof. According to Eq. (12) in the main paper, we have $I(S\mid\mathbf x')=U_S\cdot C_S(\mathbf x')$. Hence, we have

$$|\mathbb E_\epsilon[I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]|=|U_S|\cdot|\mathbb E_\epsilon[C_S(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]|,\qquad\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]=U_S^2\cdot\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[C_S(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)].$$

Therefore,

$$\frac{|\mathbb E_\epsilon[C_S(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]|}{\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[C_S(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]}=|U_S|\cdot\frac{|\mathbb E_\epsilon[I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]|}{\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]}.$$

Then, let $A_S^{\min}=\min_S|U_S|$ and $A_S^{\max}=\max_S|U_S|$ denote the lower bound and the upper bound of the absolute value $|U_S|$ over all interactive concepts $S$, we have

$$A_S^{\min}\cdot\frac{|\mathbb E_\epsilon[I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]|}{\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]}\le\frac{|\mathbb E_\epsilon[C_S(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]|}{\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[C_S(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]}\le A_S^{\max}\cdot\frac{|\mathbb E_\epsilon[I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]|}{\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]}.$$

en.title: Exact stability bounds for fixed reference coefficients
en.overview: Integral linearity and variance scaling give $EI=U EC$ and $\operatorname{Var}I=U^2\operatorname{Var}C$. On the nonzero-denominator domain, cancellation yields $|EC|/\operatorname{Var}C=|U|\,|EI|/\operatorname{Var}I$. This uses a fixed reference $U$, rather than treating a moving Taylor sign coefficient as constant.
assumptions: The ordinary-real ratio domain has $U\ne0$ and $\operatorname{Var}C>0$, with $A_{\min}\le|U|\le A_{\max}$. An empty family also requires an extremum convention; the source does not exclude every boundary.

proof_steps.body_md: The ratio $|EI|/\operatorname{Var}I$ is nonnegative. Multiply $A_{\min}\le|U|\le A_{\max}$ by it and substitute the scaling identity to obtain both source bounds. results.original_statement_md:
Let us facilitate the poof on a regression task. Based on the conclusion in Section 2.2, we can roughly consider that training a BNN on normal samples is equivalent to training a surrogate DNN model on perturbed input samples $\mathbf x'=\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon$. Then, according to Eq. (14), the learning of the BNN on a certain input sample can be roughly represented as $\min_{\{U_S\mid S\in\Omega\}}L(\{U_S\})$, and the loss is given by
$$\begin{aligned}L(\{U_S\})&=E_\epsilon[(y^*-v(\mathbf x'))^2]\\&=E_\epsilon[(y^*-\sum_{S\in\Omega}U_SC_S(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon))^2].\quad\text{(15)}\end{aligned}$$
where $\mathbf x$ and $y^*$ denote the input sample and the ground-truth output, respectively, and $\mathbf x'=\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon$.

results.title: 阶数指标与逐层分布拟合
results.original_label: Order strength, V/K metrics; Eq.(6)–(7) distribution-fit method
results.statement_tex: V_{noise}^{(s)}=E_xE_{|S|=s}\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon I(S\mid x+\epsilon),\quad K_{noise}^{(s)}=E_xE_{|S|=s}\frac{|E_\epsilon I(S\mid x+\epsilon)|}{\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon I(S\mid x+\epsilon)}
assumptions: 原经验测量与Eq6–7替代分布拟合；稳定度需要非零方差，log-odds得分需要概率处于(0,1)。

definitions.name: 本条局部对象
definitions.body_md: $s=|S|$ 是概念阶数。$V$ 是交互方差的平均，$K$ 是均值绝对值除以方差的平均；$I_{strength}^{(s)}=E_xE_{|S|=s}|I(S\mid x)|$。权重采样版本把随机源换成 $W\sim q_\theta$。

results.original_statement_md:
To verify the sensitivity to input perturbations, we added a random perturbation $\boldsymbol\epsilon\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2\mathbf I)$ to a given input sample $\mathbf x$, where $\sigma^2=0.05^2$. Then, we used the following two metrics to measure the average variance and the average relative stability of the $s$-order interactive concepts w.r.t. the input perturbation $\epsilon$. Similarly, to verify the sensitivity to the weight uncertainty, we sampled different weights $W$ from the weight distribution $q_\theta(W)$ of the BNN, and used the corresponding metrics.
$$\begin{aligned}V_{noise}^{(s)}&=E_xE_{S\subseteq N,|S|=s}\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)],\\K_{noise}^{(s)}&=E_xE_{S\subseteq N,|S|=s}\frac{|E_\epsilon[I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]|}{\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]},\\V_{BNN}^{(s)}&=E_xE_{S\subseteq N,|S|=s}\operatorname{Var}_{W\sim q_\theta(W)}[I(S\mid\mathbf x)],\\K_{BNN}^{(s)}&=E_xE_{S\subseteq N,|S|=s}\frac{|E_{W\sim q_\theta(W)}[I(S\mid\mathbf x)]|}{\operatorname{Var}_{W\sim q_\theta(W)}[I(S\mid\mathbf x)]},\\I_{strength}^{(s)}&=E_xE_{S\subseteq N,|S|=s}|I(S\mid\mathbf x)|.\end{aligned}$$
The feature of the l-th layer is computed as follows:
$$h^{(l)}=W^{(l)}(\cdots\Phi^{(1)}(W^{(1)}\mathbf x+\mathbf b^{(1)})\cdots)+\mathbf b^{(l)}.\quad\text{(6)}$$
$W^{(l)}\in\mathbb R^{D_l\times D_{l-1}}$ and $\mathbf b^{(l)}\in\mathbb R^{D_l}$ denote the weight matrix and bias. The diagonal matrix $\Phi^{(l)}=\operatorname{diag}(\phi_1^{(l)},\ldots,\phi_{D_l}^{(l)})\in\{0,1\}^{D_l\times D_l}$ denotes binary gating states of the ReLU layer.The weight dimensions are independently Gaussian; the surrogate parameters are their means. The perturbation covariance matrices are diagonal. The objective is formulated as minimizing the following KL divergence.
$$\forall1\le l\le L,\quad\min_\Delta\mathrm{KL}(p_{BNN}(h^{(l)})\Vert p_{DNN}(\widetilde h^{(l)}\mid\Delta)).\quad\text{(7)}$$
Specifically, the average strength of the $s$-order interactive concepts was measured as $I_{strength}^{(s)}=E_x[E_{S\subseteq N,|S|=s}[|I(S\mid\mathbf x)|]]$. To compute the interaction effect $I(S\mid\mathbf x)$, we set $v(\mathbf x_S)=\log\frac{p(y=y^*\mid\mathbf x_S)}{1-p(y=y^*\mid\mathbf x_S)}\in\mathbb R$, which reflected the confidence of classifying the masked input sample $\mathbf x_S$ into the ground-truth category $y^*$. For standard DNNs, $p(y=y^*\mid\mathbf x_S)$ referred to the classification probability of the ground-truth category on the masked sample $\mathbf x_S$. For BNNs, $p(y=y^*\mid\mathbf x_S)$ was computed according to Eq. (2), where we sampled ten neural networks from the weight distribution $q_\theta(W)$ of the BNN, and computed the average classification probability over all these networks.

results.title: 类别交互的符号拆分与 Jaccard 泛化指标
assumptions: 原Appendix F经验泛化定义；类内样本集合非空，Jaccard分母非零。未给从训练误差到任意测试分布的概率界。

definitions.name: 本条局部对象
definitions.body_md: 对每个类别c及全部m阶集合 $S_1,\ldots,S_d$，向量第j项是该类别训练或测试样本的平均 $I(S_j\mid x)$。$\widetilde I=[\max(I,0)^\top,-\min(I,0)^\top]^\top\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^{2d}$ 将正负贡献分开。

results.original_statement_md:
Zhou et al. (2023) quantified the average generalization ability $g^{(m)}$ over all $m$-order interactive concepts by the similarity between interaction effects of $m$-order interactive concepts in training samples and those in testing samples:
$$g^{(m)}\overset{def}=E_c[\operatorname{sim}(\mathbf I_{train,c}^{(m)},\mathbf I_{test,c}^{(m)})].\quad\text{(18)}$$
where the vector $\mathbf I_{train,c}^{(m)}=[E_{x\in train,c}[I(S_1\mid x)],E_{x\in train,c}[I(S_2\mid x)],\ldots,E_{x\in train,c}[I(S_d\mid x)]]^\top\in\mathbb R^d$ denotes interaction effects of all $m$-order interactive concepts $[S_1,\ldots,S_d]$. The interaction effect of each concept $E_{x\in train,c}[I(S_i\mid x)]$ is averaged over different training samples in the category $c$. Accordingly, the vector $\mathbf I_{test,c}^{(m)}=[E_{x\in test,c}[I(S_1\mid x)],E_{x\in test,c}[I(S_2\mid x)],\ldots,E_{x\in test,c}[I(S_d\mid x)]]^\top\in\mathbb R^d$ denotes interaction effects of all $m$-order interactive concepts, which are averaged over different testing samples in the category $c$.

In addition, the similarity is defined as the following Jaccard similarity between non-negative elements of $\mathbf I_{train,c}^{(m)}$ and $\mathbf I_{test,c}^{(m)}$.
$$\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sim}(\mathbf I_{train,c}^{(m)},\mathbf I_{test,c}^{(m)})&=\text{Jaccard sim}(\widetilde{\mathbf I}_{train,c}^{(m)},\widetilde{\mathbf I}_{test,c}^{(m)})\\&=\frac{\|\min(\widetilde{\mathbf I}_{train,c}^{(m)},\widetilde{\mathbf I}_{test,c}^{(m)})\|_1}{\|\max(\widetilde{\mathbf I}_{train,c}^{(m)},\widetilde{\mathbf I}_{test,c}^{(m)})\|_1}.\quad\text{(19)}\end{aligned}$$
where the $2d$-dimensional vector $\widetilde{\mathbf I}_{train,c}^{(m)}=[(\max(\mathbf I_{train,c}^{(m)},0))^\top,-(\min(\mathbf I_{train,c}^{(m)},0))^\top]^\top$ is constructed to contain non-negative elements of $\mathbf I_{train,c}^{(m)}$. Similarly, $\widetilde{\mathbf I}_{test,c}^{(m)}$ is constructed based on $\mathbf I_{test,c}^{(m)}$ to contain non-negative elements. Thus, a high Jaccard similarity indicates that most $m$-order interactive concepts can be well-generalized from training samples to testing samples.

results.title: 模型、扰动与概念阶数的实证比较
assumptions: 有限实验配置与观察；所有正式物理页及无证明图表页保留在逐页清单。

definitions.name: 本条局部对象
definitions.body_md: 正文图1–4及附录C–F/H比较标准DNN、均场BNN与扰动替代DNN；样本、数据集、架构和训练准确率是实验控制变量。

results.original_statement_md:
In this section, we experimentally verified that compared to standard DNNs, BNNs were less likely to encode high-order (complex) interactive concepts. Specifically, we constructed three pairs of baseline networks for comparison.

(1) Given a trained BNN $\theta^*$, we constructed a standard DNN by setting its weights to the mean value of the weight distribution of the BNN. The standard DNN was denoted by $\psi_{\theta^*}$. Then, we compared the strength of all high-order interactive concepts between the BNN $\theta^*$ and the standard DNN $\psi_{\theta^*}$ without weight/feature uncertainty.

(2) Similarly, given a trained standard DNN $\psi^*$, we constructed a BNN $\theta_{\psi^*}$ by setting the mean value of its weight distribution to the weights of the standard DNN. We set all weight dimensions in the $l$-th layer of the BNN to share the same variance $\sigma_l^2$, where $\sigma_l^2$ was computed as the average of variances of all weight dimensions in the $l$-th layer of the previous BNN $\theta^*$. Then, we compared the strength of high-order interactive concepts between the standard DNN $\psi^*$ and the BNN $\theta_{\psi^*}$.

(3) We trained a standard DNN and a BNN with the same architecture. Then, we compared the strength of high-order interactive concepts between each pair of standard DNN $\widehat\psi$ and BNN $\widehat\theta$ when these two networks were trained to have the same training accuracy. We used the training accuracy to align the learning progress of the two networks for fair comparison.

definitions.body_md: 固定原始游戏 $g$ 与参考样本，$g_T(L)=g(L\cap T)$ 对应再遮罩样本；$U_S=I_g(S)$、$C_S(x_T)=I_{g_T}(S)/U_S$。原 unmask 的AND值也是 $\mathbf1_{S\subseteq T}$。

results.original_statement_md:
Understanding of $C_S(\mathbf x')$. Let us consider a sample $\mathbf x'$ where each input variable $x_i'$ is either masked by the reference value $r_i$ or kept unchanged as $x_i$. Then, the function $C_S(\mathbf x')$ defined above represents the binary activation state of the concept $S$ in the sample $\mathbf x'$, which is an AND relationship between all variables in $S$:
$$C_S(\mathbf x')=\bigwedge_{i\in S}\operatorname{unmask}(x_i').\quad\text{(13)}$$
where the binary function $\operatorname{unmask}(x_i')\in\{0,1\}$ checks whether the $i$-th variable $x_i'$ is masked in the sample $\mathbf x'$. If the $i$-th variable is masked, then $\operatorname{unmask}(x_i')=0$; otherwise, $\operatorname{unmask}(x_i')=1$.
results.original_proof_md: Only when all input variables in S are not masked in the sample x′, the concept S is activated, and $C_S(\mathbf x')=1$. If any input variable in S is masked, then the concept S will not be activated ($C_S(\mathbf x')=0$), yielding zero interaction effect $I(S\mid\mathbf x')=0$.
results.overview: 若 $S\subseteq T$，计算 $I(S)$ 所需的每个 $L\subseteq S$ 都满足 $L\cap T=L$，交互不变。否则取 $i\in S\setminus T$；再掩码游戏插入 $i$ 不改变任何子集输出。有限差分的 dummy 消去使 $I_{g_T}(S)=0$。所以 $I_{g_T}(S)=\mathbf1_{S\subseteq T}I_g(S)$，包括原非零输出基线。

results.original_statement_md: Theorem 2.6 proves that high-order (complex) interactive concepts have low relative stability w.r.t. perturbations $\epsilon$. In this way, we can approximately consider that the strength of encoding a concept $|U_S^*|\propto |E_\epsilon[C_S(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]/\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[C_S(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]|$ also decreases along with the order of interactive concepts. In other words, we prove that high-order interactive concepts are more difficult to be learned under perturbations $\epsilon$. Combining the conclusion in Section 2.2, we also prove that high-order interactive concepts are more difficult to be learned by the BNN.
results.original_proof_md: In fact, both Theorem 2.4 and Figure 3 have told us that $|E_\epsilon[I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]/\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]|$ significantly decreases along with the order $s=|S|$ of the interactive concept $S$. Therefore, both the lower bound and the upper bound of $|E_\epsilon[C_S(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]/\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[C_S(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]|$ in Eq. (17) decrease along with the order $s$ significantly. In this way, we can approximately consider that the strength of encoding a concept $|U_S^*|\propto |E_\epsilon[C_S(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]/\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[C_S(\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]|$ also decreases along with the order of interactive concepts. In other words, we prove that high-order interactive concepts are more difficult to be learned under perturbations $\epsilon$. Combining the conclusion in Section 2.2, we also prove that high-order interactive concepts are more difficult to be learned by the BNN.

definitions.body_md: $J_\pi$ 是同一扰动输入上的不同次数触发，$c_\pi$ 是假定固定的展开系数。先考虑有限和和有限二阶矩；原无限Taylor和与含移动符号的系数还需各自合法条件。$|S|$ 是支持阶数，而不是不同次数项的数量。

results.original_statement_md: Theorem 2.4 indicates that for an arbitrary degree $\boldsymbol\pi$ of the interactive concept $S$, $\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[J(S',\boldsymbol\pi'\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]/\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]$ increases in an exponential manner along with $|S'\setminus S|=|S'|-|S|$. Therefore, we can roughly consider that $\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]$ increases exponentially w.r.t. the order $|S|$. Furthermore, according to Lemma 2.1, $I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)$ can be re-written as the weighted sum of $J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)$. Since coefficients $U_{S,\boldsymbol\pi}$ w.r.t. different $S$ and $\boldsymbol\pi$ are usually chaotic, we can roughly consider that the sensitivity of $I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)$ also grows exponentially along with the order $|S|$ of the interactive concept $S$. In addition, Theorem 2.4 also proves the approximately exponential decrease of $\frac{E_\epsilon[J(S',\boldsymbol\pi'\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]/\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[J(S',\boldsymbol\pi'\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]}{E_\epsilon[J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]/\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[J(S,\boldsymbol\pi\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]}$ along with $|S'|-|S|$. Similarly, we can obtain that the relative stability $E_\epsilon[I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]/\operatorname{Var}_\epsilon[I(S\mid\mathbf x+\boldsymbol\epsilon)]$ decreases along with the order $|S|$.

shared_proofs.title: 共享证明：实际Gaussian幂、绝对矩与增长
shared_proofs.statement_tex: Z_i\sim N(1,q_i),\quad EJ_T=\prod_{i\in T}m_i,\quad VarJ_T=\prod_{i\in T}(m_i^2+d_i)-\prod_{i\in T}m_i^2,\quad E Z_i^{k_i}\ge1
assumptions: 有限独立Gaussian坐标及自然次数；所有矩/L2从法则得到。正方差/增长子结论另用q_i>0、k_i>0及非空不交旧/新增支持。

definitions.body_md: $J_T=\prod_{i\in T}|Z_i|^{k_i}$、$m_i=E|Z_i|^{k_i}$、$d_i=Var|Z_i|^{k_i}$。E与Var为概率积分；$Z_i=1+s_i\epsilon_i/\tau$是原坐标Gaussian的可测仿射变换。最低交互另为$U_{ref}\prod Z_i$。

shared_proofs.overview: Gaussian随机量Y的map-law给任意有限p的Lp。对正整数k选p=2k，用范数实幂变换得 $|Y|^k\in L^2$；k=0为常数1。坐标可测变换保留独立，实际乘积也L2，Fubini产品积分给其均值/方差公式。这使用已发布dyn-shared-independent-residual的真实产品证明，不重复建立形式矩代数库。

proof_steps.title: 从Gaussian法则取得所有幂的L2
proof_steps.body_md: Gaussian随机量Y的map-law给任意有限p的Lp。对正整数k选p=2k，用范数实幂变换得 $|Y|^k\in L^2$；k=0为常数1。坐标可测变换保留独立，实际乘积也L2，Fubini产品积分给其均值/方差公式。这使用已发布dyn-shared-independent-residual的真实产品证明，不重复建立形式矩代数库。

proof_steps.title: 由反射与无原子证明实际量化条件
proof_steps.body_md: 对 $Z\sim\mathcal N(1,q)$，反射 $Z\mapsto2-Z$ 同律。二项式展开中 $z^k+(2-z)^k\ge2$：令 $t=z-1$，奇次项相消、偶次项非负，常数项为2。积分得 $EZ^k\ge1$；逐点 $|z|^k\ge z^k$ 给 $E|Z|^k\ge EZ^k\ge1$。任意 Gaussian 整数幂均 L2。若 $q>0,k>0$ 且绝对幂方差为零，则它几乎处处为常数；其每个水平集最多两个点，与 Gaussian 无原子矛盾，故方差严格正。独立乘积公式继而给非空积的正方差。

proof_steps.title: 分解不交支持并比较实际增长比
proof_steps.body_md:
记 $a=EA$、$b_B=EB$、$v_A=\operatorname{Var}A$、$v_B=\operatorname{Var}B$。支持不交且坐标独立给 $EAB=ab_B$ 与 $\operatorname{Var}(AB)=v_A(b_B^2+v_B)+a^2v_B$。在上述域 $a\ge1,b_B\ge1,v_A>0,v_B>0$，所以 $\operatorname{Var}(AB)/v_A>b_B^2$。令 $p=\prod_{i\in S\prime\setminus S}EZ_i^{\pi_i\prime}$，有 $b_B\ge p\ge1$，从而原方差下界成立。原 Theorem2.3 的错误精确矩替换不再作为推理前提。

由于期望均正，$K_{S\prime}/K_S=b_Bv_A/\operatorname{Var}(AB)<1/b_B\le1/p\le1$。实际 Lean 用整个旧/新增坐标 Gaussian 家族的积分证明两项不等式，所有正方差与矩下界均已由分布律消去，不假设待证结论。$S=\varnothing$ 时 $J_S=1$，$\sigma=0$ 时全部触发恒1；原比值均含0分母。源文未给该边界的实数约定，因此不将 Lean 的总除法零值作为作者约定。

proof_steps.title: 适配有符号最低交互与原绝对触发
proof_steps.body_md: 最低交互用固定参考幅值乘 $\prod_i(1+s_i\epsilon_i/\tau)$，无需截尾，其均值/方差为 $U_{ref}$ 与 $U_{ref}^2[(1+q)^s-1]$。另一方面原绝对触发逐坐标严格满足 $|s_i\tau+\epsilon_i|/\tau=|1+s_i\epsilon_i/\tau|$（$s_i^2=1,\tau>0$）。仿射map-law给均值1的Gaussian因子，加入σ正条件后实际产品增长定理直接适用。F08 PaperBayesian显式适配；F10后续复用同一共享库，但保留其原J矩错误。

en.scope: Actual Gaussian finite Lp, folded-product moments, integer signed-moment lower bounds, non-atomic nondegeneracy and original absolute-trigger growth all compile. Zero boundaries and unrestricted DNN Taylor expansion lie outside the conditional shared claim.

en.title: Shared proof: actual Gaussian powers, folded moments and growth
en.overview: A Gaussian map-law gives Lp for every finite p. For positive integer k, choose p=2k and apply the norm power transform to obtain $|Y|^k\in L^2$; k=0 gives constant one. Measurable coordinate transforms preserve independence, the actual product is L2, and Fubini factorization gives its moments. This reuses the published actual-product proof dyn-shared-independent-residual rather than duplicating a formal moment-algebra library.
assumptions: Finite independent Gaussian coordinates and natural degrees, with all moments/L2 derived from laws. Positive variance and growth additionally use q_i>0,k_i>0 and nonempty disjoint old/added supports.

definitions.body_md: $J_T=\prod_{i\in T}|Z_i|^{k_i}$, $m_i=E|Z_i|^{k_i}$ and $d_i=Var|Z_i|^{k_i}$. E and Var are probability integrals. The source coordinates give measurable affine factors $Z_i=1+s_i\epsilon_i/\tau$. The lowest dividend separately equals $U_{ref}\prod Z_i$.

en.proof_scope: Actual Gaussian finite Lp, folded-product moments, integer signed-moment lower bounds, non-atomic nondegeneracy and original absolute-trigger growth all compile. Zero boundaries and unrestricted DNN Taylor expansion lie outside the conditional shared claim.

proof_steps.title: Obtain L2 of every power from Gaussian laws
proof_steps.body_md: A Gaussian map-law gives Lp for every finite p. For positive integer k, choose p=2k and apply the norm power transform to obtain $|Y|^k\in L^2$; k=0 gives constant one. Measurable coordinate transforms preserve independence, the actual product is L2, and Fubini factorization gives its moments. This reuses the published actual-product proof dyn-shared-independent-residual rather than duplicating a formal moment-algebra library.

proof_steps.title: Prove quantitative conditions using reflection and non-atomicity
proof_steps.body_md: For $Z\sim\mathcal N(1,q)$, reflection $Z\mapsto2-Z$ preserves the law. The binomial expansion gives $z^k+(2-z)^k\ge2$: with $t=z-1$, odd terms cancel, even terms are nonnegative and the constant term is two. Integration yields $EZ^k\ge1$. Pointwise $|z|^k\ge z^k$ gives $E|Z|^k\ge EZ^k\ge1$. Every Gaussian integer power is L2. If $q>0,k>0$ and the absolute power had zero variance, it would be almost surely constant. Each level set contains at most two points, contradicting the absence of Gaussian atoms. Its variance is therefore positive; the independent-product formula gives positive variance for every nonempty product.

proof_steps.title: Split disjoint supports and compare actual growth ratios
proof_steps.body_md:
Write $a=EA$, $b_B=EB$, $v_A=\operatorname{Var}A$ and $v_B=\operatorname{Var}B$. Disjoint supports and independent coordinates give $EAB=ab_B$ and $\operatorname{Var}(AB)=v_A(b_B^2+v_B)+a^2v_B$. On the stated domain, $a\ge1,b_B\ge1,v_A>0,v_B>0$, so $\operatorname{Var}(AB)/v_A>b_B^2$. For $p=\prod_{i\in S\prime\setminus S}EZ_i^{\pi_i\prime}$, we have $b_B\ge p\ge1$, proving the source variance lower bound. The incorrect exact moment replacement in Theorem 2.3 is not used as a premise.

All means are positive, so $K_{S\prime}/K_S=b_Bv_A/\operatorname{Var}(AB)<1/b_B\le1/p\le1$. Actual Lean integrals of the complete old/added Gaussian coordinate family prove both inequalities, with positive variances and moment lower bounds discharged from distribution laws. If $S=\varnothing$, then $J_S=1$; if $\sigma=0$, all triggers equal one. Both cases give zero denominators. The source supplies no ordinary-real convention there, and Lean’s total division is not treated as an author convention.

proof_steps.title: Adapt the signed lowest dividend and original absolute trigger
proof_steps.body_md: The lowest dividend is a fixed reference amplitude times $\prod_i(1+s_i\epsilon_i/\tau)$, giving exact untruncated mean $U_{ref}$ and variance $U_{ref}^2[(1+q)^s-1]$. The original absolute trigger instead satisfies $|s_i\tau+\epsilon_i|/\tau=|1+s_i\epsilon_i/\tau|$ when $s_i^2=1,\tau>0$. The affine map-law gives mean-one Gaussian factors, and positive noise makes the actual-product growth theorem applicable. PaperBayesian explicitly adapts F08; F10 reuses the same library while retaining its original J-moment errors.

shared_proofs.title: 共享证明：独立特征损失的唯一全局最优
assumptions: 固定有限两两独立L2随机特征，均值ai、严格正方差di；Gaussian实例从map-law消去矩前提。

definitions.body_md: 有限索引 $i$ 对应作者概念 $S$，$C_i$ 是固定的随机特征函数，$w_i$ 对应作者优化变量 $U_S$，$y^*$ 是固定标签。$a,d,w\in\mathbb R^k$；矩阵 $K=\operatorname{diag}d+aa^\top$。$L(w)=E(y^*-\sum_iw_iC_i)^2$ 是原期望平方损失。

shared_proofs.overview: 中心化 $\eta_i=C_i-a_i$，两两独立性与有限 L2 给 $E\eta_i=0$ 和交叉协方差0。于是 $L(w)=(y^*-a^\top w)^2+\sum_i d_iw_i^2=(y^*)^2+w^\top Kw-2y^*a^\top w$。这是原随机特征的积分恒等式，不预设正规方程。
shared_proofs.proof_scope: 实际积分损失展开、对角加外积正定、显式正规方程及完成平方唯一全局最优均已证明。仅作为明确模型内的公共结论，不解决原零方差域或BNN替代近似。

proof_steps.title: 将真实损失展开为均值误差与方差罚项
proof_steps.body_md: 中心化 $\eta_i=C_i-a_i$，两两独立性与有限 L2 给 $E\eta_i=0$ 和交叉协方差0。于是 $L(w)=(y^*-a^\top w)^2+\sum_i d_iw_i^2=(y^*)^2+w^\top Kw-2y^*a^\top w$。这是原随机特征的积分恒等式，不预设正规方程。

proof_steps.title: 验证显式候选与正定性
proof_steps.body_md: $d_i>0$ 时对任意非零 $h$，$h^\top Kh=\sum_id_ih_i^2+(a^\top h)^2>0$。设 $t=\sum_i a_i^2/d_i\ge0$、$\lambda=y^*/(1+t)$，令 $w_i^*=\lambda a_i/d_i$。直接计算 $a^\top w^*=\lambda t$，故 $(Kw^*)_i=d_iw_i^*+a_i(a^\top w^*)=a_i\lambda(1+t)=y^*a_i$。无需 Cramer 行列式的省略步骤。

proof_steps.title: 完成平方并消去Gaussian实例的矩条件
proof_steps.body_md: $Kw^*=y^*a$ 与正定K给 $L(w)-L(w^*)=(w-w^*)^\top K(w-w^*)>0$ 对每个不同w成立。因此是真正唯一全局最优。在额外给定 $C_i\sim N(a_i,d_i)$ 的独立Gaussian实例中，map-law直接证明L2、均值ai、方差di，代入同一积分损失定理；不是将这些矩作为希望成立的假设。F08用固定概念触发，F10用Gaussian概念特征；不同原命题的错误或域限制各自在paper adapter保留。

lean.scope: Actual integral-loss expansion, positivity of the diagonal plus outer product, explicit normal equations and a completed-square unique global optimum are proved. This is a stated within-model shared result, not a resolution of zero-variance domains or BNN surrogate approximation.

en.scope: Actual integral-loss expansion, positivity of the diagonal plus outer product, explicit normal equations and a completed-square unique global optimum are proved. This is a stated within-model shared result, not a resolution of zero-variance domains or BNN surrogate approximation.

en.title: Shared proof: unique global optimum of independent-feature loss
en.overview: Center $\eta_i=C_i-a_i$. Pairwise independence and finite L2 give $E\eta_i=0$ and zero cross-covariances. Thus $L(w)=(y^*-a^\top w)^2+\sum_i d_iw_i^2=(y^*)^2+w^\top Kw-2y^*a^\top w$. This is an integral identity for the actual random features, not an assumed normal equation.
assumptions: Fixed finite pairwise independent L2 random features, means a_i and strictly positive variances d_i; Gaussian instances discharge moments from map-laws.

definitions.body_md: The finite index $i$ corresponds to a source concept $S$. Each $C_i$ is a fixed random feature, $w_i$ is source optimization variable $U_S$, and $y^*$ is the fixed label. Vectors $a,d,w\in\mathbb R^k$ give matrix $K=\operatorname{diag}d+aa^\top$. The source expected squared loss is $L(w)=E(y^*-\sum_iw_iC_i)^2$.

en.proof_scope: Actual integral-loss expansion, positivity of the diagonal plus outer product, explicit normal equations and a completed-square unique global optimum are proved. This is a stated within-model shared result, not a resolution of zero-variance domains or BNN surrogate approximation.

proof_steps.title: Expand the actual loss into mean error and variance penalty
proof_steps.body_md: Center $\eta_i=C_i-a_i$. Pairwise independence and finite L2 give $E\eta_i=0$ and zero cross-covariances. Thus $L(w)=(y^*-a^\top w)^2+\sum_i d_iw_i^2=(y^*)^2+w^\top Kw-2y^*a^\top w$. This is an integral identity for the actual random features, not an assumed normal equation.

proof_steps.title: Verify the explicit candidate and positive definiteness
proof_steps.body_md: If $d_i>0$, every nonzero $h$ satisfies $h^\top Kh=\sum_id_ih_i^2+(a^\top h)^2>0$. Put $t=\sum_i a_i^2/d_i\ge0$, $\lambda=y^*/(1+t)$ and $w_i^*=\lambda a_i/d_i$. Directly, $a^\top w^*=\lambda t$, so $(Kw^*)_i=d_iw_i^*+a_i(a^\top w^*)=a_i\lambda(1+t)=y^*a_i$. No omitted Cramer-determinant argument is needed.

proof_steps.title: Complete the square and discharge moments in Gaussian instances
proof_steps.body_md: The equation Kw*=y*a and positive definiteness give $L(w)-L(w^*)=(w-w^*)^\top K(w-w^*)>0$ for every different w, proving an actual unique global optimum. In an independent Gaussian instance C_i~N(a_i,d_i), map-laws directly give L2, means a_i and variances d_i and then the same integral-loss theorem applies. These moments are not assumed merely because they are wanted. F08 uses fixed concept triggers and F10 Gaussian concept features; each adapter retains its own original errors or domain limits.

shared_proofs.title: 共享证明：实际再遮罩游戏的交互支持
assumptions: 任意有限原始游戏与固定掩码；归一化子结论另用非零参考交互，线性比值重构另用所用参考系数非零。

definitions.body_md: 固定原始游戏 $g$ 与参考样本，$g_T(L)=g(L\cap T)$ 对应再遮罩样本；$U_S=I_g(S)$、$C_S(x_T)=I_{g_T}(S)/U_S$。原 unmask 的AND值也是 $\mathbf1_{S\subseteq T}$。

shared_proofs.overview: 若 $S\subseteq T$，计算 $I(S)$ 所需的每个 $L\subseteq S$ 都满足 $L\cap T=L$，交互不变。否则取 $i\in S\setminus T$；再掩码游戏插入 $i$ 不改变任何子集输出。有限差分的 dummy 消去使 $I_{g_T}(S)=0$。所以 $I_{g_T}(S)=\mathbf1_{S\subseteq T}I_g(S)$，包括原非零输出基线。
shared_proofs.proof_scope: 掩码支持律对所有有限游戏严格成立，包括任意b；归一化与线性重构的非零条件在声明中显式保留。

proof_steps.title: 先证明掩码交互的精确支持律
proof_steps.body_md: 若 $S\subseteq T$，计算 $I(S)$ 所需的每个 $L\subseteq S$ 都满足 $L\cap T=L$，交互不变。否则取 $i\in S\setminus T$；再掩码游戏插入 $i$ 不改变任何子集输出。有限差分的 dummy 消去使 $I_{g_T}(S)=0$。所以 $I_{g_T}(S)=\mathbf1_{S\subseteq T}I_g(S)$，包括原非零输出基线。

proof_steps.title: 非零归一化等于AND判定
proof_steps.body_md: 实际支持律除以非零参考I_g(S)，得到 $I_{g_T}(S)/I_g(S)=\mathbf1_{S\subseteq T}$；空支持也按实际b保留，若b=0则该归一化空触发不在比值域。该共享命题完全说明非零条件，不把原零系数定义问题当已解决。

proof_steps.title: 以真实当前交互线性重构
proof_steps.body_md: 对当前游戏h和固定参考系数族U，若所用U_S非零，逐项 $U_S(I_h(S)/U_S)=I_h(S)$；对子集求和及Möbius重构得h(T)。这不要求h与参考g相同，也不保证固定经验稀疏族对所有新输入支持完整。
